exam_set.title: Practice Set 2
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 12, Practice Set 2

questions.jp: オブジェクト指向におけるクラスとインスタンスとの関係のうち、適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Obujekuto shikō ni okeru kurasu to insutansu to no kankei no uchi, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a class and an instance in object-oriented design?

options.label: ア
options.jp: インスタンスはクラスの仕様を定義したものである。
options.romaji: Insutansu wa kurasu no shiyō o teigi shita mono de aru.
options.en: An instance defines the specification of a class.

options.label: イ
options.jp: クラスの定義に基づいてインスタンスが生成される。
options.romaji: Kurasu no teigi ni motozuite insutansu ga seisei sareru.
options.en: Instances are created based on a class definition.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 一つのインスタンスに対して、複数のクラスが対応する。
options.romaji: Hitotsu no insutansu ni taishite, fukusū no kurasu ga taiō suru.
options.en: Multiple classes correspond to one instance.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 一つのクラスに対して、インスタンスはただ一つ存在する。
options.romaji: Hitotsu no kurasu ni taishite, insutansu wa tada hitotsu sonzai suru.
options.en: Only one instance exists for one class.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A class is a cookie cutter or blueprint; an instance is one actual cookie or house made from it. The blueprint defines data and behavior, but it is not every real object. In this question, creation goes from the class definition to individual objects. One class can create many instances with different values. This is the object-oriented class-to-instance relationship.

Technical breakdown:
A class defines attributes and operations shared by a category of objects. Instantiation creates concrete objects from that definition. Normally one class can generate many instances, and each instance has its own state.

Japanese keywords to remember:
クラス = kurasu = class
インスタンス = insutansu = instance
生成される = seisei sareru = be created

Why the best solution works:
イ correctly states the direction: the class definition exists first, and instances are generated from it.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
The relationship is reversed; the class defines the specification used by instances.
ウ:
An ordinary instance is an occurrence of its class, not a single object simultaneously defined by several unrelated classes.
エ:
A class can generate zero, one, or many instances.

Memory trick:
Class is cookie cutter; instances are cookies.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: オブジェクト指向において、あるクラスの属性や機能がサブクラスで利用できることを何というか。
questions.romaji: Obujekuto shikō ni oite, aru kurasu no zokusei ya kinō ga sabukurasu de riyō dekiru koto o nan to iu ka.
questions.en: In object orientation, what is it called when a subclass can use a class's attributes and functions?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Imagine a new employee receiving standard abilities from their department without rewriting every procedure. A child class can likewise receive attributes and methods from a parent class. The question says a subclass can use features defined by another class. That differs from hiding details, replacing a method, or using one interface for several behaviors. The FE concept for this parent-to-child hand-down is inheritance.

Technical breakdown:
Inheritance lets a subclass reuse and extend attributes and operations defined by a superclass. It expresses an is-a relationship and supports reuse. Override, encapsulation, and polymorphism are related but different concepts.

Japanese keywords to remember:
継承 = keishō = inheritance
属性 = zokusei = attribute
サブクラス = sabukurasu = subclass

Why the best solution works:
ウ names the mechanism that makes superclass features available to a subclass.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Override replaces an inherited operation with subclass-specific behavior.
イ:
Encapsulation bundles data and operations and hides internal details.
エ:
Polymorphism allows the same interface to produce class-dependent behavior.

Memory trick:
Inheritance: child receives from parent.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: オブジェクト指向におけるカプセル化を説明したものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Obujekuto shikō ni okeru kapuseruka o setsumei shita mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which statement explains encapsulation in object orientation?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 同じ性質をもつ複数のオブジェクトを抽象化して、整理すること
options.romaji: Onaji seishitsu o motsu fukusū no obujekuto o chūshōka shite, seiri suru koto
options.en: Abstract and organize multiple objects with the same properties.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 基底クラスの性質を派生クラスに受け継がせること
options.romaji: Kitei kurasu no seishitsu o hasei kurasu ni uketsugasaseru koto
options.en: Pass properties of a base class to a derived class.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: クラス間に共通する性質を抽出し、基底クラスを作ること
options.romaji: Kurasu-kan ni kyōtsū suru seishitsu o chūshutsu shi, kitei kurasu o tsukuru koto
options.en: Extract common properties between classes and create a base class.

options.label: エ
options.jp: データとそれを操作する手続を一つのオブジェクトにして、データと手続の詳細をオブジェクトの外部から隠蔽すること
options.romaji: Dēta to sore o sōsa suru tetsuzuki o hitotsu no obujekuto ni shite, dēta to tetsuzuki no shōsai o obujekuto no gaibu kara inpei suru koto
options.en: Combine data and procedures that operate on it in one object and hide their details from outside the object.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Think of a vending machine: you press a button, while its money checks and release rules stay hidden inside. An object likewise keeps data together with the procedures allowed to handle it. Outside code uses a defined interface instead of changing private details directly. This question asks for both bundling and hiding, not a parent-child relationship. The FE concept is encapsulation, a protective boundary around state and operations.

Technical breakdown:
Encapsulation combines state with operations and exposes a controlled interface while hiding implementation details. Outside code uses public operations instead of directly depending on internal representation, reducing coupling and protecting invariants.

Japanese keywords to remember:
カプセル化 = kapuseruka = encapsulation
隠蔽する = inpei suru = conceal
手続 = tetsuzuki = procedure

Why the best solution works:
エ includes both essential parts: bundling data with its procedures and hiding their internal details from external users.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Grouping similar objects describes classification or abstraction.
イ:
Passing base-class properties to a derived class is inheritance.
ウ:
Extracting common properties into a base class is generalization.

Memory trick:
Capsule = data plus methods, protected inside.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: オブジェクト指向プログラミングの特徴のうち、異なるクラスのオブジェクトを同一のインタフェースで操作したときに、操作対象クラスに応じた異なる動作を可能にすることを何と呼ぶか。
questions.romaji: Obujekuto shikō puroguramingu no tokuchō no uchi, kotonaru kurasu no obujekuto o dōitsu no intafēsu de sōsa shita toki ni, sōsa taishō kurasu ni ōjita kotonaru dōsa o kanō ni suru koto o nan to yobu ka.
questions.en: In object-oriented programming, what allows objects of different classes to behave differently according to their class when operated through the same interface?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Give the command “speak” to a dog, a person, and a voice assistant. The command is the same, but each receiver acts according to its own kind. Programs can similarly call one interface on objects from different classes and obtain class-specific behavior. This question asks for that same-command, different-result ability. The FE concept is polymorphism: one operation takes many forms.

Technical breakdown:
Polymorphism presents a common interface while dispatching an operation to the implementation belonging to the object's actual class. Client code can treat several types uniformly without hard-coding class checks.

Japanese keywords to remember:
多相性 = tasōsei = polymorphism
同一のインタフェース = dōitsu no intafēsu = same interface
異なる動作 = kotonaru dōsa = different behavior

Why the best solution works:
エ exactly describes one interface producing class-specific behavior at runtime.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Delegation asks another object to perform responsibility; it does not itself define same-interface class-specific dispatch.
イ:
Inheritance reuses and extends superclass definitions but is not the requested behavior.
ウ:
Composition constructs an object from contained objects.

Memory trick:
One message, many forms = polymorphism.

Correct answer: エ

questions.jp: UMLにおける図の長方形の中に記述するものはどれか。
questions.romaji: UML ni okeru zu no chōhōkei no naka ni kijutsu suru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: What is written inside the rectangle shown in the UML diagram?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A UML class diagram is a labeled map of types. Each rectangle is a card for one kind of thing, such as Customer or Order. Its top compartment names the class, while other compartments may list attributes and operations. The figure points inside such a rectangle, not to a relationship line. The FE rule is that this position contains the class name.

Technical breakdown:
A class is drawn as a rectangle, commonly divided into compartments for class name, attributes, and operations. Association information belongs on connecting lines, while use cases are drawn as ellipses.

Japanese keywords to remember:
クラス図 = kurasu zu = class diagram
クラス名 = kurasu mei = class name
関連 = kanren = association

Why the best solution works:
イ identifies the basic content of the rectangular class symbol shown in the diagram.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
An association name is written near the line connecting classes.
ウ:
Aggregation is a relationship shown with a diamond, not a name placed as the class identity.
エ:
A use-case name is written inside an ellipse in a use-case diagram.

Memory trick:
Rectangle is class; ellipse is use case.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: UML2.0において、オブジェクト間の相互作用を時系列に表す図はどれか。
questions.romaji: UML 2.0 ni oite, obujekuto-kan no sōgo sayō o jikeiretsu ni arawasu zu wa dore ka.
questions.en: In UML 2.0, which diagram represents interactions between objects in chronological order?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Picture people exchanging messages during a call. To understand it, place participants across the page and read messages downward in time order. A UML sequence diagram does this for objects: vertical position represents time and arrows represent messages. The question's decisive phrase is chronological interaction. The FE concept matching an object-message timeline is the sequence diagram.

Technical breakdown:
Sequence diagrams place participants horizontally and time vertically. Message arrows show the order in which objects interact, so they are designed specifically for time-ordered collaboration.

Japanese keywords to remember:
相互作用 = sōgo sayō = interaction
時系列 = jikeiretsu = chronological order
シーケンス図 = shīkensu zu = sequence diagram

Why the best solution works:
ウ visualizes which object sends each message and in what temporal order.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
An activity diagram models control or work flow.
イ:
A component diagram models software components and dependencies.
エ:
A state-transition diagram models changes in one object's state caused by events.

Memory trick:
Sequence means message order over time.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: UMLにおける振る舞い図の説明のうち、アクティビティ図のものはどれか。
questions.romaji: UML ni okeru furumai zu no setsumei no uchi, akutibiti zu no mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which description of a UML behavioral diagram describes an activity diagram?

options.label: ア
options.jp: ある振る舞いから次の振る舞いへの制御の流れを表現する。
options.romaji: Aru furumai kara tsugi no furumai e no seigyo no nagare o hyōgen suru.
options.en: Represent the flow of control from one behavior to the next.

options.label: イ
options.jp: オブジェクト間の相互作用を時系列で表現する。
options.romaji: Obujekuto-kan no sōgo sayō o jikeiretsu de hyōgen suru.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: システムが外部に提供する機能と、それを利用する者や外部システムとの関係を表現する。
options.romaji: Shisutemu ga gaibu ni teikyō suru kinō to, sore o riyō suru mono ya gaibu shisutemu to no kankei o hyōgen suru.
options.en: Represent system functions provided externally and their relationships with users or external systems.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 一つのオブジェクトの状態がイベントの発生や時間の経過とともにどのように変化するかを表現する。
options.romaji: Hitotsu no obujekuto no jōtai ga ibento no hassei ya jikan no keika to tomo ni dono yō ni henka suru ka o hyōgen suru.
options.en: Represent how one object's state changes with events or the passage of time.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Imagine approving an expense: submit it, check it, branch if details are missing, then approve or reject. An activity diagram shows this movement from one action to the next and can include choices or parallel work. This question asks for that workflow description. Message timelines, external functions, and event-driven states use other diagrams. The FE concept is the UML activity diagram.

Technical breakdown:
Activity diagrams model control and object flows among actions. They support decisions, merges, forks, joins, and start/end nodes, making them suitable for workflows and business processes.

Japanese keywords to remember:
アクティビティ図 = akutibiti zu = activity diagram
制御の流れ = seigyo no nagare = control flow
振る舞い = furumai = behavior

Why the best solution works:
ア states the defining purpose of an activity diagram: showing control flow from one behavior to the next.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
Chronological object interaction describes a sequence diagram.
ウ:
External functions and actors describe a use-case diagram.
エ:
Event-driven changes in one object's state describe a state-machine diagram.

Memory trick:
Activity diagram = workflow of actions.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: UMLのダイアグラムのうち、インスタンス間の関係を表現するものはどれか。
questions.romaji: UML no daiyaguramu no uchi, insutansu-kan no kankei o hyōgen suru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which UML diagram represents relationships between instances?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A class diagram is a blueprint; an object diagram is a photograph of actual things at one moment. It might show customer Alice linked to order 123, rather than only Customer and Order types. This question asks about relationships between instances, meaning real objects created from classes. Workflow and use-case diagrams show different subjects. The FE snapshot for instances and links is an object diagram.

Technical breakdown:
A class diagram describes types and possible relationships; an object diagram instantiates those types and shows concrete instances, attribute values, and links. It therefore represents instance-level structure.

Japanese keywords to remember:
インスタンス間 = insutansu-kan = between instances
オブジェクト図 = obujekuto zu = object diagram
関係 = kankei = relationship

Why the best solution works:
イ is specifically defined as a structural snapshot of instances and their links.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
An activity diagram represents workflow and control flow.
ウ:
A component diagram represents deployable software components and dependencies.
エ:
A use-case diagram represents actors and externally visible system functions.

Memory trick:
Class diagram is blueprint; object diagram is snapshot.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: UMLのクラス図のうち、汎化の関係を示したものはどれか。
questions.romaji: UML no kurasu zu no uchi, hanka no kankei o shimeshita mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which UML class diagram shows a generalization relationship?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 自動車と車検証を、両端の多重度が1の実線で結んだ図
options.romaji: Jidōsha to shakenshō o, ryōtan no tajūdo ga ichi no jissen de musunda zu
options.en: A diagram connecting Automobile and Vehicle Inspection Certificate with a solid line having multiplicity 1 at both ends.

options.label: イ
options.jp: スポーツカーから自動車へ、白抜き三角形の矢印を付けた実線で結んだ図
options.romaji: Supōtsukā kara jidōsha e, shironuki sankakkei no yajirushi o tsuketa jissen de musunda zu
options.en: A diagram connecting Sports Car to Automobile with a solid line ending in a hollow triangular arrowhead.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 自動車とタイヤ及びエンジンを、黒いひし形を付けた実線で結んだ図
options.romaji: Jidōsha to taiya oyobi enjin o, kuroi hishigata o tsuketa jissen de musunda zu
options.en: A diagram connecting Automobile to Tires and Engine with solid lines ending in filled diamonds.

options.label: エ
options.jp: ドライバから自動車へ、破線の矢印で結んだ図
options.romaji: Doraiba kara jidōsha e, hasen no yajirushi de musunda zu
options.en: A diagram connecting Driver to Automobile with a dashed arrow.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Generalization means “is a kind of.” A Sports Car points toward Automobile because every sports car is an automobile. UML draws this with a solid line ending in a hollow triangle at the broader parent. In the choices, ignore multiplicities, diamonds, and dashed arrows, then find that pattern and direction. The FE concept is generalization from subclass to superclass.

Technical breakdown:
UML generalization is drawn with a solid line and a hollow triangular arrowhead pointing to the general classifier or superclass. The Sports Car-to-Automobile is-a relationship matches both the meaning and notation.

Japanese keywords to remember:
汎化 = hanka = generalization
白抜き三角形 = shironuki sankakkei = hollow triangle
実線 = jissen = solid line

Why the best solution works:
イ uses the correct hollow-triangle notation and points from the specialized Sports Car class to the general Automobile class.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
A plain solid line with multiplicities represents an association.
ウ:
A filled diamond represents composition, a strong whole-part relationship.
エ:
A dashed arrow represents a dependency.

Memory trick:
Hollow triangle points upward to the general parent.

Correct answer: イ
